seite.untertitel: Your free 3-step guide to protecting your identity, plus how this AI clone was made.
start: Agree on a safe word. Pick a word with family and close colleagues that you never post anywhere. If a call, voice note or video asks for money, passwords or urgent help, ask for the word. A clone can copy your face and voice, but not a secret it never saw.

Check the source before you believe it. Who posted it first? Find the original account and the full video, run a reverse image search on a frame, and drop the file into the free Content Credentials checker (link below). Missing credentials prove nothing, but when they are there, they show where a file came from.

Protect and claim your identity. Turn on two-factor login, keep accounts private where you can, and search your own name now and then. If an account pretends to be you, report it right away (Instagram link below) and warn your followers in a story.
seite.was_es_ist: The person in this reel was never filmed saying these words. It is HeyGen Avatar 6, an AI avatar model: you give it a photo and a short recording of yourself talking, and it turns any script into a video of "you" speaking it. Face, voice and lip movement are generated.
kann: Makes a talking video of you from one photo plus a short recording (HeyGen asks for at least 15 to 30 seconds).
Picks up your voice from that recording, so the clone speaks with your voice.
Renders every frame in native 2K; you can export in 1080p or 2K.
In HeyGen's own test, people picked the avatar as the real recording 42.2% of the time (HeyGen's research, not an independent test).
seite.kosten: Your first Avatar 6 video is free, no credit card needed. After that it runs on credits; paid plans start at $29 a month (600 credits). Prices from heygen.com, 18 Nov 2026.

seite.untertitel: Edit and restore photos with a text prompt using Higgsfield's Sunburst image model.
seite.was_es_ist: Marketing Studio Image 2.5 Sunburst is an image model from Higgsfield. It creates images from a text prompt or edits images you provide. It is offered through the Higgsfield API, and the docs do not say whether it is open source.
kann: Create images from a text prompt
Edit images from up to 16 public image URLs
Output in 1k, 2k or 4k resolution
Choose from nine aspect ratios, such as 1:1 or 16:9
Set quality from low to max
Use marketing presets with prompt enhancement

anwendungen.text: You could give the model a link to a scanned old photo. Then ask it in the prompt to remove cracks and stains and sharpen the details.

anwendungen.titel: Edit a picture with a prompt
anwendungen.text: You could supply an image URL and describe the change you want in plain text.
You could create an image with a 16:9 or 21:9 aspect ratio from a text description.
You could set the resolution to 4k and the quality to high for a detailed result.

start: Open an image model that edits photos (link below).
Upload your photo.

Paste this prompt: “Restore this old damaged photograph: remove the cracks, stains and fading, repair the missing areas, and sharpen the soldier's face and uniform while keeping his exact face, pose and clothing. Keep it a natural 19th-century portrait with clean tonal contrast and soft studio light, and add no text.”
seite.kosten: Check the official site for current pricing. You need a Higgsfield API key to use the model.

seite.untertitel: Turn a photo of yourself into a new look with one text prompt.
seite.was_es_ist: GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst is an image model from OpenAI, hosted on Replicate. It makes images from a text prompt and edits images you pass in. OpenAI describes it as its image model for detailed work. The page does not say whether it is open source.
kann: Generates images from a text prompt
Edits images you pass in
Accepts one or more reference images
Choose aspect ratio, e.g. 1:1 or 16:9
Choose quality level from low to max
Create up to 10 images per call

anwendungen.text: You could upload a photo of yourself and ask for a 1920s film star look, while telling the model to keep your face recognizable.
You could pick an aspect ratio like 1:1 or 16:9 to fit the place where you want to share the picture.
You could create up to 10 images in one call and pick the one you like best.
You could pass in more than one reference image and ask the model to combine them into a new picture.

start: Open an image model that edits photos (link below).
Upload your photo.

Paste this prompt: “Transform this photo into a black-and-white 1920s silent film star portrait: dramatic studio lighting, soft vignette, vintage film grain, a slicked-back period hairstyle and a dark tuxedo with a bow tie. Keep his face, dark hair and beard exactly recognizable, and add no text.”
seite.kosten: Price depends on the quality setting and no flat per-image price is listed; you can also pass your own OpenAI key to pay OpenAI directly.

seite.untertitel: Teach Claude a task once and let it repeat the task the same way.
seite.was_es_ist: Agent Skills are folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads dynamically to do specialized tasks better. Anthropic keeps a public repository with example skills. Many skills in the repo are open source under Apache 2.0.
kann: Teach Claude specific tasks in a repeatable way
Bundle instructions, scripts and resources in one folder
Define each skill in a SKILL.md file
Examples from art and music to testing web apps
Install skills in Claude Code with plugin commands
Use pre-built skills and upload custom ones via the Claude API

anwendungen.text: You could write a skill with your own instructions so Claude handles a recurring task the same way each time.
You could try the example skills for art, music and design as a starting point for your own ideas.
You could use a testing-focused example skill to have Claude check a web app.
You could copy the template, write a SKILL.md with a name and description, and add your own instructions.

start: Open the anthropics/skills repository on GitHub
In Claude Code, run /plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills
Install a set, e.g. /plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills
Or use the example skills on a paid Claude.ai plan, where they are already available
To build your own, copy the template and write a SKILL.md
seite.kosten: The repo is free to view, but the sources only say the example skills are available on paid Claude.ai plans, so you need a Claude account; check the official site for current pricing.

seite.untertitel: An open source AI agent that can use your real iPhone for you.
seite.was_es_ist: Poki lets AI agents operate a real iPhone, the way a person would. It is an independent open source project by Joseph Zhou and contributors. The code is under the AGPL-3.0 license.
kann: Operates a real iPhone, with no jailbreak and no extra hardware
Takes plain-language tasks, like searching in Chrome
Accepts tasks through iMessage or Telegram
Works as an MCP server for clients like Claude Code and Codex
Remembers past tasks and runs repeat tasks faster

anwendungen.text: You could ask Poki to search a topic in Chrome on your iPhone and summarize the top result.
You could send Poki a request over iMessage and get a progress note back when it is done.
You could connect Poki MCP to Claude Code or Codex so your agent can reach your iPhone.
You could run the same kind of task again and let Poki use what it remembered from earlier runs.

start: Check you have a Mac, an iPhone, a USB data cable and an Apple Account
Get Poki from the GitHub repository (git clone, then run ./bin/setup)
Run npm start and keep it running
Connect your iPhone and tap Trust when asked
Sign in to your model account or add an API key, then send a task
seite.kosten: Poki itself is open source and the page lists no price, but you need your own model account or API key (such as Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini) and its fees.

seite.untertitel: Run your own team of AI bots from a free, open source chat app.
seite.was_es_ist: OpenMausBot (also called MausBot) is an open source alternative to Grok Bot. It gives you a team of AI bots in a chat app on your own computer. It is made by Milind Soni and contributors, and it is licensed under Apache 2.0.
kann: Give each bot a job, a model and its own computer
Switch a bot's model mid-conversation
Ask for your approval before bots act
Connect apps like Gmail, Slack, GitHub and Notion
Run work on a schedule or by webhook
Run bots on your own machine with local data

anwendungen.text: You could create a bot that helps plan your day or drafts an email. You review the result before anything is sent.
You could connect Gmail and set up a bot to sort incoming messages. It asks for your approval before it acts.
You could connect GitHub and give a bot the job of working on bugs. You allow or deny each step.
You could set a bot to run on a schedule and keep an eye on competitors. You choose which model it uses.

start: Download the desktop app for your computer from the official site
Install and open the app
Connect one provider, such as Claude Code or Codex
Create your first bot: pick a name, engine and model
Send a small task and review the result
seite.kosten: The app is free and open source, but you need your own AI account or API key, and that provider's fees and limits apply. Optional cloud plans start at $15/month.
